findings.problem: Says a child may sit in front if over 10 OR at least 145 cm. The rule (old executive regulation, fine row in the MR 178/2017 table) bans the front seat for a child aged 10 or under OR shorter than 145 cm, so both conditions must be met (older than 10 AND at least 145 cm). As written, a tall 8-year-old would seem allowed.
findings.evidence: Search summaries of the rule text: 'عدم السماح للطفل من سن العاشرة فما دون، أو من يقل طوله عن 145 سم، بالجلوس في المقعد الأمامي' (Al Khaleej 2022-04-21 https://www.alkhaleej.ae/2022-04-21/ ; Emarat Al Youm 2020-08-05 https://www.emaratalyoum.com/local-section/accidents/2020-08-05-1.1382928); Excellence Driving car-seat law page says both benchmarks must be met

findings.problem: Key is right (back seat) but the explanation repeats the OR condition (over 10 or 145 cm). The ban applies if the child is 10 or under OR shorter than 145 cm, so both are needed to sit in front.

findings.evidence: q_safety.json safety-emergency-022 and safety-card-035 (RTA safe driving guide: 50 m); research/law.md S45 (SDI handbook p. 111: about 100 m)

findings.problem: The right option says 'الحبس والغرامة' but art. 38 allows jail and/or a fine (أو بإحدى هاتين العقوبتين). The explanation already says so, so the option should match it. The Arabic text's 1 year maximum was confirmed (English translation says 2 years), and the note is correct.
findings.evidence: Art. 38 Arabic text as quoted in search results for Emarat Al Youm 2024-10-28 (https://www.emaratalyoum.com/local-section/other/2024-10-28-1.1892803): 'بالحبس مدة لا تزيد على سنة والغرامة التي لا تقل عن 50,000 درهم ولا تزيد على 100,000 درهم أو بإحدى هاتين العقوبتين'

Hours and prices in the card and in law-dubai-specific-004 were confirmed: free 1 to 6 am, AED 6 at peak, AED 4 off-peak, from 31 Jan 2025.

cross_file: Warning triangle distance: q_law law-accidents-015 and law-card-030 (SDI about 100 m, both exams) vs q_safety safety-emergency-022 and safety-emergency-025 (RTA 50 m, Dubai). safety-card-035 already reconciles the two; the q_law patches above align them.
Phone 800 + 4, emergency vehicle 3000/6/30 and 3-hour accident reporting are consistent across q_law, q_safety and q_rules (no contradictions found).
unresolved: Minimum age in practice (law-law-003, law-card-002): the law says 17 and the note says institutes still apply 17.5 and 18 (KT June 2025). A later Khaleej Times piece, 'UAE minimum driving licence age lowered: 17-year-olds line up to get permits', suggests permits for 17-year-olds may now be issued (plan: learner permits from late 2025, licences from early 2026), but it was undated and could not be fetched (egress blocked). The lead should re-check whether RTA and SDI now issue licences at 17, and update the note.
Hit-and-run with injuries (art. 38): the Arabic text says 1 year maximum and the English translation says 2 years. Confirmed the Arabic wording from a search snippet and kept the item's note as is.

Sharjah discount exclusions (law-card-039, law-sharjah-specific-006, both medium): search summaries of Gulf News July 2025 confirm red light, phone, excessive speeding, sudden stopping, truck and pedestrian offences are among 40 excluded violations, and that 35% covers the fine, impound period, storage and late fees. Confidence could be raised to high; the article itself was not fetchable.

Not verified (egress blocked for gulfnews, khaleejtimes, uaelegislation, alliedlegals): fine for not moving cars after a minor accident in Dubai itself; MR 178 storage fee cap (50 per day, max 3000). Checked the rest of the numbers against search snippets and 2026 aggregator lists (speed bands, red light 1000/12/30, phone 800/4, seatbelt 400/4, 24 points and 3/6/12 months, probationary 6 months then cancellation plus 1 year, 8-point course once a year under 24, Dubai release fees 100k/50k/10k, 6000 unpaid fines, 3-hour reporting) and found no conflicts.
